resources.string: Permissions and observed status
Guided setup opens Android permission screens. You decide what to allow. Accessibility can read screen content and perform phone actions you request; overlay text can be visible to others.
No setup request has started. Status was read from this device.
Guided setup is in progress. Return from each system screen to continue.
This attempt ended. Read the individual statuses below; retry only with another tap.
An earlier setup was interrupted. Nothing was requested again; review status and tap Start to retry.
Status was read again; no permissions were requested.
Microphone access was read again after the system response.
Notification permission was read again after the system response.
The system permission is still denied or could not be observed. Continue with other steps; tap Start again to retry later.
Returned from system settings. Actual settings were read again; an open screen is not a grant.
This system settings screen is unavailable. Other steps continue; try again manually later.
A system request could not open. No grant was assumed; other steps continue.

Microphone permission
Needed to capture speech only when you separately start voice. This screen never records audio.
Notification runtime permission
Android 13 and newer ask before app notifications can be posted. Older versions do not need this runtime prompt.
Notifications enabled
Notification permission and enabled delivery are separate system signals; neither proves a notification was delivered.
App accessibility service allowed
Enabling this app service in Android settings permits assistive phone control. You must choose; this screen does not perform any action.
Accessibility service connection
A live instance is observed separately from OS authorization; it does not prove a phone action worked.
Draw over other apps allowed
Optional for a floating status display, not required for voice-only use. You decide in Android settings.
App floating overlay opt-in
The app preference is separate from Android overlay permission. This screen never turns it on or renders an overlay.
Voice listening service
Whether the listening service reports itself active. This does not prove that a request or spoken answer worked.
App control consent
The saved app consent is separate from accessibility authorization. This screen does not change it.
MCP service instance
A present service instance is only a lifecycle observation, not proof that MCP is working or authorized.
No voice capture, MCP command, accessibility action or overlay rendering is exercised here. Permissions and instance presence never establish end-to-end success.
